business_problem: Bpifrance needed to replace fragile nightly batch chains and a rigid enterprise data model that delayed consumption by up to five days, created central bottlenecks across 700 applications and 1,500 databases, and prevented the bank from delivering true real-time views of contracts, customer interactions, and operational data.
solution_summary: Bpifrance modernized its data architecture around a “Data In Flight” model built with Confluent Kafka and MongoDB Atlas. Producers publish business events in their own domain models instead of forcing them into a single enterprise schema, and consumers adapt the data locally. Kafka serves as the shared event backbone and immutable log, while the “Knowledge In Flight” service flows those events directly into MongoDB where every field is immediately searchable without destructive transformation. A companion graph database stores historical versions and relationships, and a central API gateway exposes the resulting data products to teams across the bank. This architecture let more than 240 agile teams work autonomously while preserving end-to-end traceability, giving Bpifrance a real-time, 360-degree view over contracts, payments, and customer activity without the maintenance burden and data loss of its previous batch and warehouse designs.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores searchable operational records arriving from event streams without forcing them into a single rigid schema.

solution_components.name: Confluent Kafka
solution_components.role: Acts as the bank-wide event backbone and immutable distribution channel for real-time business data.

data_flow: Domain teams publish business events to Confluent Kafka in their own models, the Knowledge In Flight service lands those events in MongoDB for immediate search and consumption, and downstream applications query contracts, payments, and customer activity through APIs and complementary graph views.
business_outcome: Bpifrance achieved true real-time processing, decentralized data ownership, and a consolidated 360-degree operational view, while supporting 7 million contracts, 450 million MongoDB documents, and low-footprint analytics that improve CRM timelines, recommendation quality, and regulatory traceability.
metrics: 1.5 billion nodes in its graph database
architecture_clues: Bpifrance lets producers publish in their own business models instead of a single enterprise schema.
MongoDB stores immutable, untransformed event data while a graph database keeps relationships and history.
The architecture satisfies right-to-be-forgotten requests by deleting a user-specific encryption key.
evidence_quotes: Using Confluent Kafka and MongoDB Atlas, Bpifrance built 'Knowledge In Flight' to let producers publish data in real time via their own models.
The system required extracting nightly data dumps into a massive 400 TB shared database, resulting in delays of up to five days before data could be consumed.
With MongoDB, all fields are searchable immediately. And no transformation is applied—real business data is ingested exactly as it’s produced.
The organization has now achieved a global, detailed 360-degree view of its operations, encompassing 450 million MongoDB documents and 1.5 billion nodes in its graph database.
